churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, config and the section pattern are each behind a single seam, so a framework upgrade would mostly touch package.json. The two things that will age badly are the untyped RPC boundary (field renames fail silently in six consumers) and error caching that treats transient failures as permanent 404s.

findings.issue: apiFetch caches every promise for the process lifetime, including rejections/failed responses resolved to null; a transient API hiccup permanently poisons the cache and renders NotFound (with a 404 status) for perfectly valid Pokémon, moves, abilities and types.
findings.suggestion: Only memoize successful responses (or add a TTL/soft revalidation), and distinguish 'resource not found' (null) from 'fetch failed' (throw) so routes can render an error state instead of a permanent 404.

findings.issue: The whole app is untyped JSX: query result shapes (e.g. getPokemonPage's ~20-field object) cross the server/client RPC boundary with no type contract, so renaming a field in data.js silently breaks any of the six route consumers.
findings.suggestion: Adopt TypeScript (SolidStart v2 templates are TS-first) or at minimum JSDoc-typed return types for the five exported queries in lib/data.js.

findings.issue: Query-string handling is hand-rolled in three places (updateParams, pageHref, and a `?game=` string template) using URLSearchParams directly.
findings.suggestion: Use the router's own setSearchParams (already imported from useSearchParams in the Pokémon page) or one shared buildHref helper so adding a query param touches one place.

findings.issue: Anchor scrolling is hand-rolled via onMount + window.location.hash + scrollIntoView; it only fires on mount, so client-side navigations that include #moves (e.g. the game <select> at line 124) depend on undocumented router behaviour to scroll.
findings.suggestion: Use the router's scroll/hash handling or a createEffect on location.hash so the scroll works on every navigation, not just the first.

findings.issue: The root wraps routes only in Suspense; there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere, so a query that throws during client-side navigation renders a broken route with no fallback.
findings.suggestion: Add an ErrorBoundary around props.children (or per-route) with a fallback that links back home.

findings.issue: .vinxi/ is listed but SolidStart v2 no longer uses Vinxi — stale v1-era boilerplate.

summary: This app is on SolidStart v2's current stable stack to an unusual degree: vite.config.ts with the solidStart()/nitro() plugins, router queries with "use server", route preloads, and the documented MetaProvider/Suspense root — on @solidjs/start 2.1.0 and @solidjs/router 1.0.1 released within days of this review, with zero dependencies beyond the six the framework requires. Platform usage is strong (fetch, URLSearchParams, native form controls, custom properties, modern grid layout). The two things that will age poorly are the untyped RPC boundary between lib/data.js and six route files, and apiFetch caching failures forever, which turns a transient API hiccup into a permanent 404.
